title: Spray a perfume tester on a blotter strip held in its line, then lay the strip on the tray touching nothing else
keywords: hold a thin card in a spray's line
instruction: Try the perfume on a blotter strip. Take one strip from the stand and hold it upright, tip up, about 15 cm in front of the tester's nozzle. With the other hand, turn the tester on its display block to aim the nozzle at the strip's tip and press the spray from above, so the perfume wets the strip across its full width within 4 cm of its tip. Then lay the strip on the tray and move both hands clear. The strip may touch only the grippers and the tray; leave the other strips standing in the stand and the tester on its block.
context: Most people have tried a perfume at a shop's tester by spraying it on a paper blotter strip. One hand holds the strip upright, its tip about 15 cm from the nozzle, while the other turns the tester on its display block to aim it and presses the actuator from above through its full stroke. Only the result is scored: the perfume leaves a mark across the strip's full 12 mm width within 40 mm of its tip, landed while a gripper held the strip up in the air, out of the stand, after the tester had been turned on its block; the strip ends up on the tray, having touched nothing but the grippers and the tray since it left the stand; the other strips still stand; and the tester stays upright on its block. The difficulty is physical: a thin card held still in the spray's line while the other hand turns and presses a 281 g bottle standing on a small block, then carried and laid down without brushing the counter, the stand, the block or the bottle.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y left); heights above the table top. A 40 x 60 cm glass counter top (60 cm along y), 1 cm thick, lies on the table centred at x 35, y 0. On it: a 10 x 10 cm white acrylic display block, 5 cm high, at x 35, y 8. On the block stands a Chanel N°5 Eau de Parfum 100 mL spray tester (named for identification only) with its cap off: glass 7.6 x 3.8 cm and 7.4 cm high, 9.8 cm to the top of its actuator, 281 g (retail listing). Its nozzle is 14 cm above the counter and faces +x, away from the robot. Its actuator, 2 cm across, fires one spray when pressed down through its stroke. In the simulation the stroke (4 mm, firing at 90% of it), the force at full stroke (10 N), a 30 degree spray cone and its 22 cm reach are settings; a real trial uses the real tester and its own perfume, which darkens the card where it lands. At y -17: a clear acrylic blotter stand, 18 x 3 cm and 2.5 cm high, holds five white blotter strips (130 x 12 mm, 0.5 mm card, 0.5 g) upright in a row along x, 3.5 cm apart from x 32 to x 46, each in its own 2 cm deep slot; the top end is the tip. At x 22, y -20: a white melamine tray, 12 x 18 cm (18 along y), with a 4 mm floor and a 1 cm rim. Friction (static/dynamic): card 0.6/0.5, the tester's glass 0.5/0.4, counter, block, stand and tray 0.5/0.4. Both arms start at their home poses, grippers open. Simplified: the spray is a cone of droplet rays that darken the strip where they land.
scoring: Scored by effect only; how the strip is held, its distance from the nozzle, the number of presses and the order of steps are not scored. Steps are cumulative; each needs the ones below it. 0.5: one strip carries the spray's mark across its full 12 mm width within 40 mm of its tip, from spray that landed while a gripper held the strip up in the air and the tester had been turned at least 45 degrees on its block from its start (nozzle facing +x): the gripper's jaws shut on it, the strip at least 1 cm clear of the stand, and its lowest point more than 1.5 cm above the counter, above the tray's 1 cm rims (real trial: the perfume darkens the card where it lands; read with a ruler from the tip on a photo taken against a light within 5 s of the press; the strip in the gripper and where it was at the press, on the wrist, top and side cameras). 0.75: that strip lies on the tray floor, inside its rim and out of the grippers (end frame of the top camera, or a photo). 1.0: that, and from the moment it left the stand the strip touched nothing but the grippers and the tray: no contact with the counter, the stand, the display block, the tester or its nozzle, or another strip (frame by frame on the top camera and on a side camera at counter height looking along the counter past the stand, block and tray); the other four strips never left their slots or tipped past 20 degrees (top camera); the tester stands upright on its block, tilted under 10 degrees (a square against its side on the end photo); both grippers are at least 3 cm from the strip and from the tester's faces (a ruler on the end photo); and the strips and the tester move under 1 mm over the last 1 s (two photos 1 s apart). 0, latched: the tester falls over or comes down off its block onto the counter or the floor (lifting it and setting it back is allowed), or any strip reaches the floor (top and side cameras). Spray that wets the other strips or the tray is not scored. In the simulation a contact is any point of the strip within 2 mm of a surface, counted once the strip is 1 cm clear of the stand; a mark is a 4 x 6.5 mm cell hit by 2 or more droplets.
fidelity: Rigid bodies at 240 Hz on the GPU. Each blotter strip is a rigid 0.5 mm card that does not bend. The spray is a 30 degree cone of 2,000 straight droplet rays reaching 22 cm, cast each time the actuator passes 90% of its 4 mm stroke (10 N spring; all settings); a 4 x 6.5 mm card cell hit by 2 or more turns dark. A real spray carries further and may wet the standing strips: not scored. Contact: a strip point within 2 mm of a surface. A real trial uses the real tester.
reset_notes: Nothing is random (object_jitter=0): the same layout every trial. Between real trials, put fresh dry strips in all five slots, and wipe the counter, block and tray dry.
